[Participants]
Priya Nair (Head of Operations, Nordwind), Marta Lindqvist (Commercial Director, Nordwind), Tom De Vries (IT Lead, Nordwind Rotterdam), Sanne Bakker (ATCON), Deepak Rao (ATCON)

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:00:04]
Thanks everyone. Before we get into anything technical I'd like to just understand the business. Priya, can you walk me through what Nordwind actually does?

[Priya Nair @ 00:00:19]
Sure. We're a freight forwarder. Sea and road mostly, some air but it's marginal. Head office is Bergen, we've got Oslo and a Rotterdam office. Customers come to us with a shipment and we arrange it end to end — booking the carrier, the customs paperwork, the warehousing if they need it. The bit that's hurting is the front end of that. Getting a price back to the customer.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:00:52]
Tell me about that.

[Priya Nair @ 00:00:55]
A customer emails us, or phones, and says I've got forty pallets going from Bergen to Rotterdam, week after next, what's it going to cost. And then somebody on the quotation desk has to go and work that out. And working it out means opening a spreadsheet, looking up the sea freight rate for that lane, adding the haulage at both ends, adding the customs clearance fee, checking whether there's a surcharge running this month, and typing it all into an email. That takes about two days. Sometimes three.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:01:37]
Two days from the enquiry landing to the customer having a number?

[Priya Nair @ 00:01:42]
Yes. And it isn't two days of work. It's twenty minutes of work sitting in a queue for two days.

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:01:52]
And we lose business over it. That's the part I care about. If a customer sends the same enquiry to us and to two competitors and we come back third, we don't get the booking. It doesn't matter that our price was good. I don't have a hard number for you but my sense is it's a meaningful share of what we quote.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:02:19]
We'll want to come back to that number. Who does the quoting?

[Priya Nair @ 00:02:24]
The quotation desk. Erik runs it out of Bergen. There are people in Oslo and Rotterdam doing the same job for their local lanes.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:02:36]
And how many people would end up using a system like this?

[Priya Nair @ 00:02:41]
About forty users all in, once you count the sales people and the branches. Not everyone's quoting but everyone wants to see where a quote has got to.

[Tom De Vries @ 00:02:56]
I'd want to push back slightly on forty. That's everyone with a login to anything. The people actually building quotes is a much smaller group.

[Priya Nair @ 00:03:08]
Well, they all need to see it.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:03:11]
Noted, we'll firm that up. Tom, what have they got today, systems-wise?

[Tom De Vries @ 00:03:18]
The quoting itself is a Microsoft Access database from about 2011. We call it NordQuote. It holds the rate cards and it prints the quote document. It doesn't really do anything else. Then there's Winfreight, which is the TMS. That's where a booking lives once it's actually a booking. Winfreight is the system of record for anything operational. And there's a lot of Excel. More than I'd like to admit.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:03:55]
Does NordQuote talk to Winfreight?

[Tom De Vries @ 00:03:59]
No. Somebody re-keys it. When a quote is accepted, whoever's on the desk opens Winfreight and types the whole thing in again.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:04:12]
How often does that go wrong?

[Priya Nair @ 00:04:16]
Often enough that we check. Erik reconciles the accepted quotes against Winfreight every Friday afternoon. He finds two or three a week where something's off — wrong container type, wrong incoterm, a price that doesn't match what we sent the customer.

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:04:38]
And when the price doesn't match, we honour what we sent. So that's straight off the margin.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:04:47]
Marta, you mentioned approvals earlier.

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:04:51]
Everything goes through me before it leaves the building. Every quote.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:04:58]
Every quote, or quotes above a value?

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:05:02]
Every quote. That was a decision we took after a bad year in 2019 where we underpriced a lot of work. It's the right control but I'll be honest, I'm the reason some of those two days are two days. I was on a flight last Tuesday and nothing went out until Wednesday evening.

[Priya Nair @ 00:05:26]
It's not sustainable. Marta shouldn't be reading a quote for four hundred euros of groupage.

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:05:34]
No. But somebody has to look at the four hundred thousand euro tender.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:05:41]
That's a useful distinction. What happens to a quote after you send it?

[Priya Nair @ 00:05:47]
Honestly? Not much. It's in the sent items of whoever sent it. If the customer comes back a week later and asks about it, we search Outlook. We don't have a proper view of what's outstanding. I couldn't tell you right now how many live quotes we have or what they're worth.

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:06:12]
Which means I can't forecast. I'd like to be able to say to the board, we have this much in the pipeline, historically we win this proportion of it.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:06:26]
Do you know your win rate today?

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:06:29]
No.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:06:32]
What about the customer's side of it — do they ever see anything other than the email?

[Priya Nair @ 00:06:39]
No. Email only. Some of the bigger accounts have asked for a portal and we've always said it's on the roadmap.

[Tom De Vries @ 00:06:50]
It has been on the roadmap since I joined.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:06:55]
Is a customer portal in scope for this?

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:07:00]
Let's park it. I want the internal thing working first. If we can't get a quote out in a day, giving the customer a window onto that isn't going to help us.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:07:14]
Agreed. Last one from me for today — what does good look like? If we come back in a year and this has worked, what's different?

[Priya Nair @ 00:07:26]
A quote goes out the same day. Erik isn't reconciling anything on a Friday. And when Marta asks what's outstanding, somebody can answer her in ten seconds instead of two hours.

[Marta Lindqvist @ 00:07:44]
And I'm looking at the quotes that matter, not all of them.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:07:50]
That's helpful. We'll pull the process apart properly next session.

[Participants]
Erik Sørensen (Quotation Desk Lead, Bergen), Priya Nair (Head of Operations), Tom De Vries (IT Lead), Johan Bakker (Sales, Oslo), Sanne Bakker (ATCON), Deepak Rao (ATCON)

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:00:08]
Erik, I'd like you to talk us through a quote from the moment it arrives. Don't tidy it up.

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:00:16]
All right. It arrives in the shared mailbox, quotes@nordwind. That's the front door. Everything comes in there — new enquiries, replies to old quotes, carrier rate updates, spam. First job in the morning is somebody triages that mailbox. Works out what's actually an enquiry and who should take it. That's usually me, takes about forty minutes.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:00:47]
How do you assign it?

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:00:50]
I drag it into a subfolder with the person's name on it. That's the assignment. There's no other record of it. Then whoever's got it has to work out whether we've quoted this customer for this lane before. Because if we have, we should be consistent. So they search Outlook. That's genuinely the process — search your own sent items and hope.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:01:22]
How long does that take?

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:01:25]
Ten minutes if you find it. Twenty if you don't and you go and ask the person who might have done it. Then the pricing. Open NordQuote, find the lane, pull the base rate. Then you go to the carrier rate sheet, which is a spreadsheet on SharePoint, because NordQuote's rates are only updated quarterly and the carriers change theirs monthly.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:01:56]
So NordQuote's rates are out of date.

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:02:00]
Always. Everyone knows not to trust them. You use it for the structure and you get the actual numbers from the sheet.

[Tom De Vries @ 00:02:10]
Which is the root of most of what's wrong here, honestly. There's no single place where a rate is correct.

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:02:19]
Then haulage at both ends, which depends on the postcode, and that's a different sheet. Customs clearance is a flat fee unless it's out of the EEA. Then whatever surcharges are live — there's a bunker adjustment that moves monthly and a congestion surcharge on Rotterdam that's been on for eight months. You put all that in an Excel template, it works out the total, you copy it into an email.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:02:53]
And then it goes to Marta.

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:02:56]
Then it goes to Marta. In an email. With the spreadsheet attached. She replies approved, or she asks a question, and if she asks a question that's another day gone because now it's a conversation.

[Johan Bakker @ 00:03:14]
From my side that's where it dies. I've got a customer on the phone asking where their quote is and I have no idea. I email Erik, Erik emails Marta, Marta's in a meeting. I've started just quoting things myself for the small stuff. I know I shouldn't.

[Priya Nair @ 00:03:36]
You shouldn't.

[Johan Bakker @ 00:03:38]
I know. But a customer isn't going to wait two days for a price on one pallet.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:03:45]
How much of the volume is small like that?

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:03:49]
Most of it by count. A big chunk of what we quote is groupage under a thousand euros. It's maybe a tenth of the value and most of the effort.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:04:03]
What about the exceptions? What breaks the standard path?

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:04:08]
Dangerous goods — that needs a different set of questions and a specialist carrier. Temperature controlled, same. Anything going out of the EEA needs the customs piece done properly rather than as a flat fee. Project cargo, which is out-of-gauge stuff, that's bespoke every time. And tenders. Where a customer says price me these sixty lanes for the year. Those take a week and there's no template for them at all.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:04:44]
How often does each of those come up?

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:04:48]
Dangerous goods, a couple a week. Out of EEA, maybe a fifth of everything. Project cargo, once a month. Tenders, a handful a year but they're most of the revenue when we win them.

[Deepak Rao @ 00:05:06]
Tom, what does Winfreight expose? If we wanted to write a booking into it from a new system.

[Tom De Vries @ 00:05:14]
I'd need to check. I know there's something because the finance integration works, but I don't know what it is or who owns it. It's a vendor product, we're on their hosted version. I'll find out. Don't build anything assuming it's easy.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:05:36]
Understood. What about the timeline? Marta mentioned peak season last time.

[Priya Nair @ 00:05:43]
Look, realistically we're looking at Q1 next year. Nothing goes live in October — October is our busiest month, we can't have people learning a new system while they're doing twice the volume. I know there's pressure from the board on this. But operationally, Q1.

[Tom De Vries @ 00:06:08]
That's not what I heard on Monday.

[Priya Nair @ 00:06:11]
Then we need to have that conversation internally before you build anything to an October date.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:06:19]
We'll flag it. Erik, one more — what would you actually want, if you could have anything?

[Erik Sørensen @ 00:06:27]
One place where a rate is right. That's it. Everything else follows from that. And I'd like to stop reconciling on a Friday. Two hours every week, and it only exists because we type everything twice.

[Johan Bakker @ 00:06:46]
I want to be able to look up a quote without emailing anybody.

[Priya Nair @ 00:06:52]
And I want to know what's sitting in the queue.

[Sanne Bakker @ 00:06:57]
Thank you. That's very clear.

[p.1 ¶1]
Nordwind Logistics AS Standard Operating Procedure — Quotation Handling Document QMS-04, version 3.2. Issued 14 January 2024. Owner: Head of Operations.

[p.1 ¶2]
1. Purpose and scope This procedure governs the preparation, approval and issue of freight quotations for all Nordwind Logistics business units. It applies to sea, road and air freight, to groupage and full-load consignments, and to both spot enquiries and contracted tender pricing.

[p.1 ¶3]
All quotations are prepared by the quotation desk, which comprises 12 staff across 3 branches: Bergen (6), Oslo (3) and Rotterdam (3). No quotation may be issued to a customer by any other function.

[p.1 ¶4]
2. Receipt of enquiry

[p.1 ¶5]
2.1 All customer enquiries are received into the shared mailbox quotes@nordwind.no. Enquiries received by telephone are entered into the mailbox by the receiving employee before any pricing work begins.

[p.1 ¶6]
2.2 The Quotation Desk Lead reviews the mailbox each working morning and assigns each enquiry to a named quotation clerk by moving the item to the clerk's designated mailbox folder.

[p.1 ¶7]
2.3 Enquiries received after 15:00 local time are assigned on the following working day.

[p.1 ¶8]
3. Preparation of the quotation

[p.1 ¶9]
3.1 The assigned clerk shall establish whether the customer has previously been quoted for the same or a comparable lane within the preceding six months. Where a prior quotation exists, the clerk shall ensure consistency of pricing basis and shall record any deviation.

[p.1 ¶10]
3.2 Base freight rates are obtained from the NordQuote rate database. Where the carrier has issued a revised tariff since the last quarterly NordQuote update, the current carrier rate sheet held on SharePoint takes precedence.

[p.1 ¶11]
3.3 The following components shall be included in every quotation where applicable: base freight, origin haulage, destination haulage, customs clearance, documentation fee, and any surcharges in force at the date of issue (bunker adjustment factor, congestion, currency adjustment).

[p.1 ¶12]
3.4 The quotation shall be prepared using the approved Excel quotation template (QMS-04-T1). Manual calculation outside the template is not permitted.

[p.1 ¶13]
3.5 Validity. Unless otherwise agreed, quotations are valid for 14 days from the date of issue. Quotations involving out-of-gauge or project cargo are valid for 7 days.

[p.1 ¶14]
4. Approval

[p.1 ¶15]
4.1 No quotation shall be issued to a customer without the prior written approval of the Commercial Director.

[p.1 ¶16]
QMS-04 v3.2 · Nordwind Logistics AS · page 1

[p.2 ¶1]
4.2 Approval is requested by forwarding the completed quotation template to the Commercial Director by email. The Commercial Director shall record approval by reply.

[p.2 ¶2]
4.3 In the absence of the Commercial Director, approval authority passes to the Managing Director. This provision is to be used only where the delay would otherwise exceed one working day.

[p.2 ¶3]
4.4 This control was introduced in November 2019 following a review of underpriced business in that financial year and shall not be varied without Board approval.

[p.2 ¶4]
5. Issue and record

[p.2 ¶5]
5.1 The approved quotation is issued to the customer by email from the assigned clerk, copying the responsible salesperson.

[p.2 ¶6]
5.2 A copy of the issued quotation is retained in the clerk's sent items. No central register of issued quotations is maintained.

[p.2 ¶7]
5.3 Where a quotation is accepted by the customer, the assigned clerk shall create the corresponding booking in Winfreight. All commercial terms shall be entered to match the issued quotation exactly.

[p.2 ¶8]
6. Reconciliation

[p.2 ¶9]
6.1 The Quotation Desk Lead shall, each Friday, compare all quotations accepted during the week against the corresponding Winfreight bookings and shall record any discrepancy on form QMS-04-F2.

[p.2 ¶10]
6.2 Where a discrepancy is identified between the price quoted to the customer and the price recorded in Winfreight, the price quoted to the customer shall stand. The Winfreight record shall be corrected.

[p.2 ¶11]
7. Exceptions

[p.2 ¶12]
7.1 Dangerous goods. Consignments classified under ADR or IMDG require completion of the dangerous goods questionnaire (QMS-11-T3) and pricing by a clerk holding current DGSA-supervised certification.

[p.2 ¶13]
7.2 Temperature-controlled consignments require confirmation of equipment availability from the carrier before a price is issued.

[p.2 ¶14]
7.3 Consignments originating or terminating outside the European Economic Area require full customs treatment. The flat clearance fee at 3.3 shall not be applied.

[p.2 ¶15]
7.4 Out-of-gauge and project cargo shall be priced individually. The quotation template is not used.

[p.2 ¶16]
7.5 Annual tender submissions are prepared by the Commercial Director with support from the quotation desk and are outside the scope of sections 2 to 5.

[p.2 ¶17]
8. Records

[p.2 ¶18]
8.1 Completed reconciliation forms QMS-04-F2 are retained for 24 months.

[p.2 ¶19]
8.2 This procedure is reviewed annually by the Head of Operations. QMS-04 v3.2 · Nordwind Logistics AS · page 2

sources.rawText:
[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 00:00–00:11]
This is Eric Sorensen, quotation desk lead at Nordwind, leaving a voice note for the Atcon team as you asked. You wanted a picture of a normal day, so let me tell you about yesterday.

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 00:11–00:22]
I came in at half past seven, sixty-one items in the shared mailbox overnight. About twenty of those were actual inquiries, the rest were carrier notices and replies

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 00:22–00:36]
to things we sent last week. It took me until quarter past eight to sort them and push them out to the desk. Then I picked up three myself. The first one, Bergen to Rotterdam for Hanseatic chemicals, took me maybe fifteen minutes of

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 00:36–00:50]
actual work. Right from the sheet, haulage both ends, the congestion surcharge that has been running on Rotterdam since November. Straight forward, but it did not go out yesterday because it needed approving and Marta was

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 00:50–01:05]
in Oslo all day, it went out this morning, so the customer waited a day and a half for fifteen minutes of work. The second one was dangerous goods, class three flammable liquids, going to Immingham.

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 01:05–01:16]
That's a different questionnaire, a different carrier list, and I have to check the packing group before I can price anything. That took most of the morning and I still have not sent it because I am waiting on the

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 01:16–01:28]
carrier. The third one I have not started. The thing I would want you to understand is that none of this is complicated work. It is not difficult to price a container.

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 01:28–01:39]
What kills us is that the information is in four places, none of them agree, and every quote has to queue behind one person's inbox before a customer can see it.

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 01:39–01:51]
And then on Friday I spend two hours comparing what we sent against what got typed into Winfreight because we type everything twice and people make mistakes when they type things twice.

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 01:51–02:01]
Last week I found three that did not match. We honor whatever the customer was told, so every one of those came off our margin. That is the job.

[call-with-erik.mp3 @ 02:01–02:03]
Call me if you want to walk through any of it.

conflicts.subject: Go-live date for the new quoting system

sideA.claim: Go-live must be before end of October; board considers this non-negotiable
sideA.quote: board signed off this morning. they want it live before peak season — that's end of October, not negotiable apparently

sideB.claim: Go-live cannot happen in October due to peak season workload; realistic target is Q1 next year
sideB.quote: Look, realistically we're looking at Q1 next year. Nothing goes live in October — October is our busiest month, we can't have people learning a new system while they're doing twice the volume. I know there's pressure from the board on this. But operationally, Q1.

conflicts.whyItMatters: This is a hard contradiction between board-mandated and operations-proposed go-live dates. Design, resourcing, and delivery plan depend critically on which timeline is binding. Building to an undetermined date creates severe project risk.
conflicts.resolutionQuestion: The board has signed off on a go-live 'before peak season — that's end of October, not negotiable apparently' (E-src_eb65fe4e-003), but operations state 'Nothing goes live in October — October is our busiest month, we can't have people learning a new system while they're doing twice the volume ... operationally, Q1.' (E-src_1855173c-026). Which date is the project to plan for: before end of October, or Q1 next year?

Manual flagging and subfolder assignments in Outlook are used to manage workload.

brief.executiveSummary: Nordwind is aiming to transform their quotation process so that quotes go out the same day, thereby increasing win rates for new business and enabling proactive management of their sales pipeline. Today, most quotes queue for days behind a manual approval process, with information fragmented across spreadsheets, email, and legacy systems, creating costly errors, lost margin, and missed opportunities. The central unknown is when the new system must launch, with the board insisting on a pre-peak season deadline and operations stating that a Q1 go-live is the only safe option; resolving this conflict is critical to setting a feasible delivery plan.

blueprint.summary: This solution streamlines the quotation process to ensure quotes are issued the same day, directly addressing all high-impact pain points by automating intake, route matching, centralizing data, and providing structured approvals. Automation targets non-judgement steps, while compliance requirements and critical approvals remain intact. Every design choice traces to stated requirements and constraints; open questions are not assumed resolved.

toBeProcess.name: Automated enquiry capture and triage

toBeProcess.rationale: System auto-matches against previous six months of registered quotes based on origin/destination/customer and flags matches. Speeds up consistency check.

toBeProcess.rationale: Guided form enforces required fields, pulls current carrier rates from single source (see Feature F3), performs auto-calculation for all components per requirements. Reduces manual copying and math errors.

toBeProcess.rationale: Once approved in system, quote auto-generates PDF and sends to customer; clerk confirms and can add custom note if needed. Ensures faster turnaround, standard template, eliminates email copy step.
